problems: Scratch directory /tmp/claude-0/work/research-ea-06-x/ held stale drafts from an earlier run of this batch (fang-guozhen, ispah-rebellion, mangyul-gungthang, principality-of-liang, zhang_wu); none had reached the mount and no report existed. They were not reused: all twelve dossiers were rebuilt from pages opened in this run, and the stale JSON drafts were deleted.

WebFetch returns a model's summary of the page, not the page text; quotation marks in notes were kept only where the summary itself quoted (a script removed the rest), so every note is a close paraphrase of a dated sentence.

Page budget: zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu cites 7 pages and zhang-shicheng-s-wu 6, over the 2-5 pages of the orchestrator note, because their wars and conquests are spread over the biography pages of their rivals; the batch opened 23 distinct pages in all.
No page opened gives an area for any of these states, so no keyframe has an infobox comparison; every shape is a circle round named cities or a province union and should be read as soft.

zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu is the Ming's first phase (same state and ruler, proclamation 23 January 1368); the colour agent should share the Ming's hue (family china) and the Ming dossier should absorb it as a rename if it starts in 1368.

The ea-06-b tibet dossier names yuan-dynasty as counterpart for its 1354 and 1358 events; they should name sakya-regime. The yuan-dynasty dossier (ea-06-a) is expected to carry the vassal events for sakya-regime, duan-governors-of-dali and zhang-shicheng-s-wu (1357-1363).
Families: Tibetan states use 'india' to match the tibet dossier, principality-of-liang-yunnan 'mongol', duan-governors-of-dali 'southeast-asia' (as kingdom-of-dali), the Red Turban states 'china'.

Rulers are given only where a page lists them (tianwan, chen-han, ming-xia, han-song, zhang-shicheng-s-wu, zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu, principality-of-liang-yunnan); fang-guozhen-s-regime, sakya-regime, ispah-rebellion, mangyul-gungthang and duan-governors-of-dali have none.
